title: EXPERIMENTAL ANALYSIS OF PERMEABLE GROYNE LAYOUTS ON MEANDERING CHANNEL FLOW

EXPERIMENTAL ANALYSIS OF PERMEABLE GROYNE LAYOUTS ON MEANDERING CHANNEL FLOW

Journal: Water Conservation and Management (WCM)
Author: Aflah Ornima, Anika Tahsin Nabila, Mahibur Alam, Md Ishmam Labib, Somaila Nanziba Rupanty, Md Osman Goni
Print ISSN : 2523-5664

ABSTRACT

Groynes are hydraulic structures designed to mitigate bank erosion, regulate flow direction, and support navigation of rivers. Among various types, permeable groynes are increasingly used in river engineering, particularly in meandering channels, to enhance flow control and sediment transport. This study investigates the effects of different permeable groyne layouts, made of wood, on velocity distribution, energy and momentum coefficients, and shear stress distribution through laboratory experiments. The experiments were conducted in an open-air facility where data were collected from 10 experimental runs across five different groyne configurations in a compound meandering channel. Velocity measurements were taken at four cross-sections, with four zones in each, under two flow depths (20 cm and 15 cm). Results indicate that setup 2 (three groynes at 41.4 cm spacing) provides the most effective velocity reduction across zones, minimizing shear stress. Energy and momentum coefficients vary with depth, with setups 2 and 4 performing optimally at 15 cm depth. Overall, setup 2 demonstrates the most favorable hydrodynamic performance, effectively managing flow characteristics and shear stress distribution. These findings offer insights for optimizing permeable groyne placement in meandering rivers to enhance riverbank protection.
